content:
- Overestimate prices after recent sentiment spikes (especially when sentiment > 0.0) — model tends to overshoot and then correct.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative and persistent — model fails to account for downward pressure.
- Lag in correction: model often lags 1–3 days in adjusting to sentiment shifts; apply a 1–2 day delay in price correction when sentiment changes direction.
- Mean reversion bias: model overreacts to short-term volatility; reduce forecast amplitude in high-volatility periods.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are consistently too high in early periods (first 5–7 days) — apply downward adjustment of 0.5–1.5% for first 7 days.
- Sentiment-weighted smoothing: if sentiment is > 0.2 for 3+ consecutive days, reduce forecast slope; if sentiment < -0.3, increase downward bias by 0.3–0.7% per day.
